newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Sundiro lands 5.1-bln-yuan order for '97.
newsitem.headline: Sundiro lands 5.1-bln-yuan order for '97.

text.p: Motorcycle producer Hainan Sundiro Motorcycle Co Ltd won purchase orders for 930,000 motorbikes worth 5.1 billion yuan at a recently-held goods fair, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Monday.

The newspaper said that despite intense competition Sundiro racked up about 1.9 billion yuan in sales on production of 350,000 motorcycles in 1996 due to the firm's success in upgrading production technology and developing new products.
A spokeswoman for Sundiro told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin that most of the 930,000 motorcycles would be delivered in 1997, with some for delivery in 1998.
The company reported net profits of 70.57 million yuan for 1995, up 26.40 percent over 55.83 million yuan in 1994.
The spokeswoman said the company expected higher post-tax profits for 1996 than 1995, but she declined to give figures.
Sundiro's 1996 interim net earnings reached 65.96 million yuan compared with the year-earlier level of 33.04 million yuan.
Sales hit 862.79 million yuan against 482.69 million yuan in 1994, with output surging 92.68 percent year-on-year to 198,754 motorcycles in 1995.
Last week, the company said in a statement that it planned to make a 2.142-for-10 rights offer and then issue 100 million B shares in 1997.
The rights offer, tentatively priced at between four and six yuan per share, would be made on the firm's current total share capital of 237.44 million shares, the statement said.
The company expected to carry out the rights plan by June 30, 1997 and added that it planned to launch an offer of 100 million B shares in 1997 after the rights offer, it said.

The firm said that if the offers were approved by the China Securities Regulatory Commission, it would use the money raised to upgrade production technology and set up a motorcycle engine venture with the Japanese firm Kawasaki Heavy Industries Ltd.
